saints.name: St. Nicholas
saints.title: Bishop of Myra
saints.shortBlurb: The fourth-century bishop of Myra whose renown for secret generosity made him, in legend and love, the patron of children and of sailors…
biography: Nicholas was bishop of Myra in Lycia, in Asia Minor, in the early fourth century, and by tradition suffered imprisonment for the faith before the peace of the Church under Constantine. Little is known of his life with certainty, but he was venerated very early for his charity, above all for the story of his secret gift of gold that saved three poor girls from ruin.

His relics were carried to Bari in southern Italy in 1087, and his fame spread through the whole Church. From his hidden generosity grew, in many lands, the beloved figure of the Christmas gift-bringer.
saints.knownFor: Secret almsgiving that made him patron of children and sailors.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 6 December
